narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The genre originated in Spain during the 1970s, following the country's democratic transition.
It was driven by a desire to modernize traditional flamenco, which had been displaced by rock-and-roll in previous decades.
Key figures like José Antonio Pulpón fostered collaborations between traditional cantaores and rock musicians, leading to the definitive break with the conservatism of the Mairena era.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: New Flamenco utilizes traditional flamenco guitar virtuosity combined with instruments such as the Peruvian cajón, transverse flute, bass, and electronic synthesizers.
The music often incorporates rhythms from jazz, blues, rock, rumba, and hip-hop, while maintaining the underlying metric structure of traditional flamenco palos.
Listen for the flamenco guitar, cajón, transverse flute, bass.
A blend of virtuosic flamenco guitar and traditional vocal techniques with modern percussion, bass, and electronic textures.

music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of New Flamenco (Spain). Instruments: flamenco guitar, cajón, transverse flute, bass, electronic instruments. Mood: fusion, rhythmic, modern, expressive. It should sound like this: A blend of virtuosic flamenco guitar and traditional vocal techniques with modern percussion, bass, and electronic textures. New melody, new arrangement: do not quote or imitate any specific recorded song; keep the idiom, the instruments, the pulse and the proportions.

rules: Original composition only — no sampling, no melody of any existing recording, no lyrics from any song.
